orientation.summary: This is Vermont's 2015 Wildlife Action Plan (SWAP), a comprehensive 10-year revision covering Species of Greatest Conservation Need (SGCN), their habitats, and threats. The document has a strong and explicit posture toward climate change, including a dedicated chapter (Chapter 3) on climate change impacts, vulnerability assessments, and conservation strategies. Range shifts are addressed directly and substantively—the document discusses northward/upslope species movements, forest community compositional change, and phenological shifts, and links connectivity conservation explicitly to enabling species range shifts under climate change. The document performs its own climate vulnerability assessment (18 species, 44 habitats) and develops conservation actions in response; it references external scientific literature extensively for climate projections and ecological impacts, and references regional collaborative programs. The document also includes appendices for species conservation reports, a landscape conservation design, a big game management plan, and a landowner wildlife habitat management guide.
